name: Iceland
summary: Act on Narcotics 65/1974: possessing or using controlled drugs is a crime; small amounts are usually fined. Bills to decriminalise personal-use amounts (2020–2023) did not pass.
callingForHelp: No specific legal protection for people who call for help in a drug emergency was found.

log.title: Lög um ávana- og fíkniefni nr. 65/1974

reg.title: Reglugerð 233/2001 um ávana- og fíkniefni (substance lists, amended 2025)

lsd.note: Controlled (Regulation 233/2001). Possession is a crime; small amounts usually end in a fine.

mushrooms.note: Psilocybin and psilocin are controlled, so mushrooms containing them are treated as illegal.

dmt.note: DMT is controlled; ayahuasca is therefore illegal.

mescaline.note: Mescaline and mescaline cacti and seeds (Echinopsis pachanoi/peruviana) are listed.

dox.note: DOB, DOM, DOET and related compounds are listed.

nbomes.note: 25I-NBOMe and many other NBOMes are listed.

cannabis.note: Illegal; small amounts usually mean arrest and a fine rather than prison. Decriminalisation bills have failed.

ketamine.note: Listed controlled substance: possession without a prescription is an offence.

dxm.note: Not on Iceland's controlled substances list (2025 version). As a medicine, its supply is pharmacy-regulated.

nitrous.note: Not a controlled substance; no specific possession offence found.

amphetamines.note: Amphetamine and methamphetamine are controlled. ADHD medicines are legal with a prescription.

alcohol.note: Legal from 20 to buy or be served; retail mainly through state-run Vínbúðin stores.

ghb/gbl.note: GHB, GBL and 1,4-butanediol are all listed controlled substances.

opioids.note: Heroin, fentanyl, oxycodone and other opioids are controlled; legal only with a prescription.

tramadol.note: Tramadol is a listed controlled substance; prescription required.

benzodiazepines.note: Listed controlled substances; legal only with a prescription.

maois.note: Medical MAOIs are prescription-only; harmala/Syrian rue are not listed. Ayahuasca is illegal (DMT).
